title: Requirement record (CCIR, FFIR or PIR)
description: One requirement, one Markdown file per record (requirements/CCIR-001.md). Requirements is the parent category; each record is exactly one of three types: CCIR (what the owner needs to know), FFIR (what the rest of the lab needs to know: friendly readiness and posture) or PIR (what we need to know about the environment or adversary). supports names one or more SO/OO/TO it serves; serves names requirements it feeds: an FFIR may serve CCIRs, a PIR CCIRs or FFIRs, a CCIR nothing (checked by homelabnext.strategy). Lifecycle: active -> answered | expired | retired. 2.0 (ADR-0019): a record is identified by its `uid` (a UUIDv7) and names its `type`; every link is a uid; the numbered `id` is gone (the number a record is shown with is computed from type, parent and sibling `order`, never stored). The record-type rules of a link (which types a parent, supports, serves or raised_by may name) are the doctrine's `hierarchy` and `links`, checked by homelabnext.strategy. 1.x records are read only by `hnx records assign-uids`, which migrates them.

parent.description: Optional: the uid of the requirement it refines (a PIR under a PIR: PIR 2.1).

order.description: Optional: the sort key among its siblings (same type, same parent). Siblings without one follow, in creation (uid) order.

cadence.description: An ISO 8601 duration (PT15M, P1W), continuous or on-change.

ltiov.description: Last time the information is of value: a date (swept to expired after it) or standing.

sirs.description: Specific information requirements the question breaks into.

indicators.description: Indicators and essential elements of information.

reviews.description: Derived from the review events (homelabnext.reviews); never written in the record file.

uid.description: A record uid: a canonical UUIDv7 (lowercase, version 7), created with the record and never changed (ADR-0019).
